In this assignment we joined the field of the employees working in 2018 from the NZ
census data to the shapefile of the provinces of NZ 

#IMPORTANT: IN THIS EXAMPLEI CHANGED THE WAY THE markdown file works with paths so that 
#the directory is not the location of the file but rather the location of the project
#if it was the location of the file then the path would have been only the .csv file name 
#because the .csv and the mark down file are in the same place. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
paid_workers_csv <- read_csv("homework/wk1/2018_paid_workers.csv")  

```
#To load the shapefile I just look for the folder and only include in my var the .shp file
#but I do need all of the other files in my folder
```{r}
library(sf)
# my data is within my homework wk1 file
nz_shape <- st_read("homework/wk1/statsnz-territorial-authority-2018-generalised-SHP/territorial-authority-2018-generalised.shp")
```
# Important to always load the library and then we can start working with it
```{r}
library(sf)
nz_shape %>% 
  st_geometry() %>%
  plot()
```

# Merging the data using the column from my csv and the column from the shp file I want to Join 
# The shp has the TA2018_V1_
# The csv has the Area_Code

# IMPORTANT: because when we used the merge function, the . stands for what was previously defined meaning the shapefile of new zealand, and then the csv. So x is for the column of the .shp and y for the csv

```{r}
nz_updated_shape <- nz_shape%>%
  merge(.,
        paid_workers_csv,
        by.x="TA2018_V1_", 
        by.y="Area_Code")
```


# Ploting the new shapefile with the new column appended
```{r}
library(tmap)
tmap_mode("plot")
# change the fill to your column name if different
nz_updated_shape %>%
  qtm(.,fill = "Paid_employee_2018")
```
# Histrogram
```{r}
hist(nz_updated_shape$Paid_employee_2018,breaks=30, main="Histogram of paid employees per Territorial Authority Area")
```
```{r}
# 1. Create a new column with the log of the values
# after the $ is the name of the column I chose (before <-)
nz_updated_shape$log_Paid_employee_2018 <- log(nz_updated_shape$Paid_employee_2018)

# 2. Plot the histogram of the new column
# In this case my new colums was called log_Paid_employee_2018
hist(nz_updated_shape$log_Paid_employee_2018,
     breaks = 30,
     main = "Histogram of log of paid employees per Territorial Authority Area")
```
# Map of the log function 
```{r}
library(tmap)
tmap_mode("plot")
# I choose to plot my log column in my shapefile
nz_updated_shape %>%
  qtm(.,fill = "log_Paid_employee_2018")
```



# Saving the new shapefile to a .gpk 
```{r}
nz_updated_shape%>% st_write(.,
  "homework/wk1/nz_paid_workers_2018.gpkg",
  layer = "Paid_workers_2018",
  delete_dsn = TRUE
)
```
# Make the connection to the gpkg

```{r}
library(readr)
library(RSQLite)

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(),dbname="homework/wk1/nz_paid_workers_2818.gpkg")
```

# list the tables inside, at the beginning it mught be empty 
```{r}
con %>%
  dbListTables()
```

# we add the csv file and then disconnect from the DB 

```{r}
con %>%
  dbWriteTable(.,
               "original_csv",
               paid_workers_csv,
               overwrite = TRUE)

con %>% dbDisconnect()
```
